summary: The lord of conflict, service and illness joins the self. BPHS gives a sickly but famous, wealthy and courageous person who is at odds with his own people; Raman and Bhavartha Ratnakara add trouble from cousins, while Raman also names military or penal careers when the lord is well aspected.

Friction with one's own people or cousins (BPHS 24.61; Bhavartha Ratnakara 5.1 with Raman's note)
Hard-working; drawn to army, prisons, medicine or healing (Raman; Braha)

Braha: thin build, special diet, difficult start in life, no fame
Rath: the 6th lord in the lagna is in the 8th from the 6th, giving disease to enemies and good health to the native
Raman, 300 Combinations no. 265 Vrana yoga: a malefic 6th lord in the lagna, 8th or 10th is a classical combination for serious illness, which Raman says must not be applied literally

by_area.personality: Adventurous and virtuous but at odds with his own people (BPHS 24.61); Rath: inimical toward his own family and self.
by_area.career: Raman: well aspected, a soldier, commander, minister of war or prison official. Braha: hard worker, medical or healing arts.
by_area.health: BPHS 24.61 and Bhavartha Ratnakara 5.1: sickly (traditional); Braha: poor health; Rath gives the opposite (good health to self).
by_area.relationships: Bhavartha Ratnakara 5.1: troubled by cousins; Raman's note adds worry from relatives' machinations.
by_area.family: Raman: lives in the maternal uncle's house; Braha: close to the maternal uncle, born to a common family.

The 6th lord in a benefic's sign and aspected by benefics (Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope p. 136: many friends)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Raman: weak and afflicted gives the criminal-conduct reading (traditional view)
Lagna lord in the lagna with the 6th, 8th or 12th lord (Raman, 300 Combinations no. 111 Rogagrastha: weak constitution)
Lagna lord and 6th lord both in the lagna, or the lagna lord in the 6th aspected by the 6th lord (Raman p. 136: trouble from relatives)
The 6th lord in a kendra joined or aspected by malefics (Phaladeepika 16.16; Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope p. 136: constant trouble from enemies)
Phaladeepika 16.19: the house occupied by the 6th lord becomes a source of enmity for the native
lagna_or_context_notes: Functional role (BPHS 34.2-7; Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope pp. 13-15; Frawley): lords of the 3rd, 6th and 11th give evil effects, and Raman ranks the 6th lord less malefic than the 11th but more than the 3rd. By lagna: Mercury (3+6) is the greatest malefic for Aries and Mars (6+11) the most malefic for Gemini (Raman); Saturn (6+7) for Leo, Jupiter (3+6) for Libra, the Moon for Aquarius and the Sun for Pisces are malefics (BPHS 34.29-44); Venus (6+11) is the only inauspicious planet for Sagittarius (BPHS 34.37). Exceptions: Jupiter (6+9) for Cancer and Mercury (6+9) for Capricorn are auspicious (BPHS 34.27, 34.39; Raman); Mars (1+6) is neutral for Scorpio (BPHS 34.35; Raman); for Taurus, Venus (1+6) is listed as a malefic in BPHS 34.23 but neutral in Raman, and Frawley says a lagna lord stays generally auspicious though tainted by the 6th; Saturn (5+6) for Virgo is neutral in Raman. For Taurus (Venus) and Scorpio (Mars) the 6th lord is the lagna lord itself; Bhavartha Ratnakara 5.8 says that when a weak lagna lord who also owns the 6th is joined by benefics, enemies turn friends.

source_views.view: Bad health, bad jobs, dishonest workers, losses through subordinates, unfortunate uncle, no sexual pleasure, plain bedding, ailments of the anus, left ear and left eye.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology: Timing of Events (1998), ch. II 2.3 (pp. 12-13) (archive.org file 'Crux Of Vedic Astrology - Timing Of Events - Sanjay Rath')
source_views.view: If the 6th lord and 12th lord conjoin, the enemy suffers losses and the native gains; in a dusthana this becomes a Vipareeta raja yoga; benefics should not join it.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology: Timing of Events (1998), ch. IX 9.3 (pp. 120-121) (archive.org file 'Crux Of Vedic Astrology - Timing Of Events - Sanjay Rath')
source_views.view: The native is inimical toward the matters of the house where the 6th lord is placed; houses counted from the 6th to its lord are promoted for the native and damaged for the enemy, the reverse for houses counted back from the lord to the 6th.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 16.16-16.19 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Malefics in the 6th, a strong 6th lord linked with the lagna lord, or the 6th lord in a kendra with malefics give lasting trouble from enemies; a lagna lord stronger than the 6th lord gives health; the 6th lord in a dusthana, weak, with a stronger lagna lord destroys enemies; the house the 6th lord occupies becomes inimical.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 34.2-7, 19-44 (tr. G.C. Sharma)
source_views.view: Lords of the 3rd, 6th and 11th give evil effects; lagna-by-lagna lists (e.g. Jupiter auspicious for Cancer, Mercury and Venus auspicious for Capricorn, Mars neutral for Scorpio, Venus the only inauspicious planet for Sagittarius).

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope Vol. I, ch. II 'Benefics and Malefics for each Lagna' and 'Yoga Karakas' (pp. 13-15)
source_views.view: Lords of the 3rd, 6th and 11th are malefic, the 11th worst, the 6th less, the 3rd least; per-lagna lists of benefic, malefic and neutral planets.

source_views.source: David Frawley, The Astrology of the Seers, 'Laws of House Rulership' and 'House Lords as Specific Significators' (pp. 157-161)
source_views.view: Lords of 3, 6 and 11 are generally inauspicious and project a more negative force than the lords of 6, 8 and 12 as houses; the lagna lord stays generally auspicious even if it also rules the 6th; the 6th lord 'promotes disease or gives power to our enemies, as that is what it rules'.

disagreements: Direct conflict: BPHS 24.72, Raman (both books) and Braha are unfavourable; Phaladeepika 6.63 and Rath's Vipareeta principle are favourable. Raman argues from practice that the favourable reading rarely holds in full.
phrasing_guidance: Frame as 'conflicts tend to dissolve' and advise mindful spending. State BPHS's harsh line only as a traditional view if needed; no moral judgements.
